Parking the whole roadmap. The roadmap has 1 of 2 committed stages complete. Stage 2 and the three Track A Ranked-list items each become one deferred item, and the roadmap retires to `specs/completed/`.

**1. Read the item schema and the current backlog** before writing anything:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md
Read specs/deferred_items.md        # may not exist yet; if so, create it
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`** under a new dated section. Each item will follow the Deferred-item schema exactly. This is the content I'll fit into it:

```
## lock-closures — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices to boat operators (parked Stage 2, Track B)
      Send boat operators an email notice within an hour of a lock closing, from the closure log's live feed.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll each 10 minutes)
      Done when: a notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (parked Ranked list, Track A, O2)
      Turn the river-level forecast into a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock, using the closure-vs-gauge curve from specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md (closures rise steeply above 3.1 m).
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop)
      Done when: a daily 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock is produced from the real forecast.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled across all 14 locks (parked Ranked list, Track A, O3)
      Fit separate closure-vs-gauge curves for all 14 locks, pooled. Stage 1 found that the four longest-record locks show close to the same curve.
      Size: about 14× Stage 1's data (Stage 1: 1.8 GB, 22 min)
      Done when: closure curves for all 14 locks, fit on the real data, are recorded with the run's measured cost.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (parked Ranked list, Track A, O4)
      Publish a static closure-history map of the canal's locks for boat operators.
      Size: about a day of work (one static map page)
      Done when: the closure-history map page exists.
```

**3. Retire the roadmap:**

```
mkdir -p specs/completed
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
```

Then add this line directly under the title in the moved file:

```
> PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Remaining stage and Ranked-list items moved to specs/deferred_items.md, § lock-closures — 2026-11-06.
```

The findings file and plan 4 stay where they are, because the deferred items cite the findings. This roadmap has no spec, methodology or critique file to retire.

**4. Commit on `main`:**

```
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended"
```

When this is done, the roadmap is closed, and nothing else is routed or handed off. The four parked items will age in the deferred backlog like any others. If funding returns, `/deferred` is the way to promote them.
